Alton Brown is making a web-based sequel to Good Eats

As someone who cooked professionally for many years, rising through the kitchen ranks, I can fairly judge Alton to be the most informative and educational TV chef I've ever seen. I hope he makes this new show easily/cheaply accessible, because pirating Good Eats is my first recommendation to poor li'l college kids that can barely make ramen.

Disclaimer: Alton is sometimes wrong. On rare occasions he's wrong so hard it goes beyond a factual level to hit a moral level. His crockpot no cheese lasagne, for instance, is not just wrong on "that's not how you comfort food" level, but becomes an offense against God himself (check the paintings, God is clearly Italian). Nonetheless, in general, Alton is a gift to anyone that wants to learn to be a better cook in their own home.

edit: other worthwhile TV chefs: Julia Child, ofc. Also Two Fat Ladies.

I love the joy he obviously has for cooking and teaching it in his show. My wife and I had a very tough year with our newest baby, and she's finally getting comfortable with getting back into the kitchen with new things again. How can I tell? Good Eats filled up our DVR one weekend.

For all their faults Emril and Mario make my list of top TV chefs as well. Michael Simon is cool too. Actually met the guy when he came in to do a demo at the restaurant I worked at at the time. He broke down a whole pig and we did a special all-pork menu that night. I got out of cooking years ago, but Alton was the one who got me into it in the first place.

Mario I haven't watched too much of, so I can't comment, but Emeril I have an issue with. He doesn't explain stuff enough. Alton's greatest strength is his constant efforts to not just deliver a recipe, but explain why you should do something, and how you can alter a recipe to your tastes. He teaches techniques. Emeril is more of an entertainer than an explainer.

Also, according to folks I know that have met/worked with him, Emeril is a major jackass IRL. I can't say anything about that personally, I've never met the guy and this is all hearsay, but that's what I've heard. (Alton actually doesn't do to well on the hearsay front either, but I freely admit that I'm biased and more willing to forgive Alton)

As for Michael Symon, that's cool as hell. I've broke down my fair share of animals, but I never got a straight on demonstration from an expert for a whole hog, it was always more just watch this guy for a day then try to do what he does. I have some land. Have some coworkers who I have taken/gone shooting with a few times. Two of them came and shot out at my land, helped set up a small range, and said they'd love to come help on it any time and go shooting. Since land is expensive and I don't get to use it as often as I want to, and I have no local friends with which to do such things, I invited them camping. Neither of them had any gear, so it was like camping with cub scouts. I had to bring everything from home. And all the guns.

Upon arrival, one of them got his sports car stuck in the field, and then unstuck. They opened their brand new flashlights, marveled at spider eyes glimmering in the dark. Explored the abandoned old house. And then it came time to head to camp. Which is 350 yards up hill through the woods with no trail. So we loaded up a big Gorilla cart with half of their gear, I put on my ruck with all of my gear, and up we went. It probably took 45 minutes. Cart overturned several times dumping beer and sleeping bags everywhere. Had to make 2 trips. On the second trip, something spilled. Gas/oil mix for the chainsaw. And an entire jar of pickle juice. They were exhausted. I noted at the top that we had my 1-man-1-woman tent, my 4-man tent, and another borrowed 5-man taj-mahal tent. Blankets. Sleeping bags. Tons of alcohol.

They immediately set up chairs at the fire. Got a fire going. It was quite dark at this point. I started setting up my tent and debated warning them.... and then decided it would be kind... "Guys, I know you want to get shit faced and relax, but you have tents you've never set up before... you should probably do that before you're drunk, tired, and cold at 4am." That was an entertaining sight...

Turns out I forgot to bring MY chair, amongst all of the packing for them. Grrr.

We talked, we drank Jack Daniels and traded beers. I had ground up some venison that morning with about 40% really good bacon, we ate burgers out of the cast iron pan. It was fantastic.

Ended up not being as cold as expected. They got to hear coyotes. Drank delicious spring water (filtered). Stayed up until 3am. Reluctantly decided this was a very "friends" thing to do and maybe I had to consider them friends...

No one wanted to shoot or do anything the next morning, they were too hungover, almost too much for eggs and bacon. Realized one of them had brought a 24 pack of Coke Zero up the mountain, and only drank 2 of them. Awesome. Ate at Taco Bell on the way back into town. Dr. Pepper was good, man.
An unextraordinary tale of taking coworkers camping
When you say you have some land - how much are we talking about? How many acres?
Without getting too specific, more than 40 and less than 70. But as a conglomeration to an unused, undeveloped, and middle of no where 200 acres.

Hmm... I'm asking because I'm looking to buy some land for camping / hunting, and I've seen some listings for around 10 acres in nice wooded areas that are also close enough to me to be relevant, but I have no idea if that's large enough to be fun / worth having.

Somewhat conventionally (not all of our reasoning was conventional), I was looking for sufficient land that our kids could feel "lost" exploring it and that if I built a house and then condos went up on the surrounding property boundaries I wouldn't be pissed. We are in hills and mountains that are heavily wooded, and we found as little as 25 acres handled this demand. For camping, I would think 10 acres would be plenty, given that most people go camping on 1000 square foot plots packed in with others. You're probably not going to get to stay up until 4am drunk and rowdy on 10 acres behind a housing development in the city limits, but it would be fine.
